rules.text: Use voriconazole as the sole test drug; comparator or co-administered drugs are not substitutes. Do not import the apramycin model or its parameters.

evidence.quote: Following the translational objective of Sou et al. (2021), we do not import the apramycin model or its parameters.

Voriconazole is the sole test drug; fluconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole, amphotericin B, caspofungin and tofacitinib appear in the sources as comparators or co-administered drugs and are not substitutes.

rules.text: Use Voriconazole_source_tables_by_species.xlsx as the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Split its mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs. rules.text: Use the secondary multi-species table only as low-confidence context or for sensitivity analysis, never as the sole basis for a species model. Keep it labelled as secondary throughout and document whether and how it is used.

rules.text: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Do not treat group means, published fitted parameters, model-predicted AUCs or digitized points as individual animals or observations. Do not invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links or missing measurements.

evidence.quote: Keep source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters, model-predicted AUCs and digitized points are not individual animals or observations.

rules.text: Keep routes, total and unbound drug, serum, plasma and free brain dialysate, and bioassay and chromatographic results separate. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; do not transfer parameters between doses or days because exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Record a justification for every conversion.

evidence.quote: Separate routes (oral gavage, intraperitoneal, IV), total versus unbound drug, serum versus plasma versus free brain dialysate, and bioassay versus chromatographic results. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats, so parameters from one dose or day do not transfer to another. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Every conversion requires a recorded justification.

rules.text: Never average the conflicting binding sources: mouse 78% bound in serum, 29.97% unbound in plasma and 67% in the secondary table; rat 64–66%. Carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

evidence.quote: Binding sources conflict (mouse 78% bound in serum versus 29.97% unbound in plasma versus 67% in the secondary table; rat 64-66%); never average them, and carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

rules.text: Select eligible systemic PK models for mouse and rat, including saturable elimination and time-dependent clearance where supported by the data. Evaluate fit and parameter identifiability, and evaluate held-out prediction where the design permits.

evidence.quote: 2. Fit animal PK. Select eligible systemic PK models for mouse and rat, including saturable elimination and time-dependent clearance where the data support them. Evaluate fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits.

rules.text: Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, metabolic clearance and justified physiological relationships, accounting for nonlinearity and autoinduction before scaling. Compare approaches with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and Cmin with uncertainty under specified IV and oral regimens, including loading doses. Do not use the rat escalating regimen designed to match a human exposure target to tune scaling.

evidence.quote: 3. Predict human PK. Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, metabolic clearance and justified physiological relationships, accounting for nonlinearity and autoinduction before scaling. Compare approaches with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and Cmin with uncertainty under specified IV and oral regimens, including loading doses, and freeze them before opening human outcomes.
The rat escalating regimen was designed to match a human exposure target; do not use it to tune scaling.

rules.text: Release the separate human reference tables only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen; freeze human predictions before opening human outcomes. Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling. Freeze the model, validation criteria, PD targets and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

evidence.quote: Human validation data are not in this package. Human reference tables (label PK parameters and statements, a healthy-volunteer IV-to-oral dose-escalation study, and a human-target column removed from a rat source) are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and Cmin with uncertainty under specified IV and oral regimens, including loading doses, and freeze them before opening human outcomes.

rules.text: Use matched isolate MICs for PD and MIC distributions for population-weighted attainment. A distribution cannot replace matched isolate MICs.

evidence.quote: Use matched isolate MICs for PD and the distributions for population-weighted attainment; a distribution cannot replace matched isolate MICs.

rules.text: For eligible data, compare fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using both ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, separately by organism and endpoint. Give all three indices equal eligibility and compare them on the same matched response records, isolate MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting. Report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that the data cannot determine a best index or target. Keep CFU-based and survival-based targets separate; a target from one organism or endpoint cannot set another.

rules.text: Do not let published ED50s, exposure indices or conclusions set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings.

rules.text: Apply the frozen model to the doses and regimens in the human reference tables. Compare predicted and observed plasma PK, including the change from single to repeated dosing. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.

evidence.quote: 5. Validate the human prediction. Apply the frozen model to the doses and regimens in the human reference tables. Compare predicted and observed plasma PK, including the change from single to repeated dosing. rules.text: Only after PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and IV and oral dosing scenarios to estimate PTA at each MIC. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty. Deliver PTA tables or curves and a feasibility conclusion; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

evidence.quote: 6. Produce PTA and assess feasibility. After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and IV and oral dosing scenarios to estimate the probability of target attainment (PTA) at each MIC. Process the MIC distributions and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty. Deliver the PTA tables/curves, feasibility conclusion and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

rules.text: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators, censored categories and test method, including EUCAST, CLSI or NCCLS. Do not interpret the EUCAST distributions as resistance rates: they were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs, and the C. albicans data are mostly truncated at 0.016 mg/L. Derive probabilities transparently, freeze the MIC distribution and never silently renormalize. Distinguish and separately report per-MIC PTA and MIC-weighted attainment.

evidence.quote: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators, censored categories and test method (EUCAST, CLSI or NCCLS). Derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution; never silently renormalize. Distinguish per-MIC PTA from MIC-weighted attainment.
Process the MIC distributions and report distribution-weighted attainment separately.

rules.text: Propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty in PTA.

evidence.quote: Propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty; group summaries cannot supply invented interindividual variability.

rules.text: Report model feasibility without presenting the result as a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability. A successful fit is not predictive validation, and human PK agreement does not validate antifungal efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps.
